outcome: No result since 26 January 2024 answers, or removes territory from, the stated question of whether GCH entails ◇_{E^{λ+}_{cf(λ)}} for every singular cardinal λ; the question remains exactly as open as it was in the frozen revision.
summary: This bullet is a precise statement of a well-known open problem of Shelah in singular cardinal combinatorics: does CH_λ (equivalently, GCH restricted to λ) entail the diamond principle ◇ on the stationary set E^{λ+}_{cf(λ)} — the set of points of λ+ with cofinality *equal to* cf(λ) — for every singular cardinal λ? This is the one cofinality class left open by Shelah's classical Theorem 1.8 (documented in Rinot's 'Jensen's diamond principle and its relatives', arXiv:0911.2151, itself pre-window), which establishes CH_λ ⟺ ◇_S for every stationary S ⊆ E^{λ+}_{≠cf(λ)} (cofinality *different* from cf(λ)). The same-cofinality case is the genuine gap, and it is what the Wikipedia bullet asks about. I searched extensively for work in the window (26 Jan 2024–present) and found substantial *adjacent* activity, but nothing that touches this exact set: (1) 'Weak diamond and PCF theory' (arXiv:2405.03142, May 2024) improves Shelah's bound on |pcf(a)| using weak diamond, a converse-flavored, unrelated direction; it does not address entailment of full diamond from CH_λ on same-cofinality sets. (2) A cluster of 2025 papers on the approachability ideal I[λ+] — Jakob–Levine ('Failure of Approachability at the Successor of the first Singular for any Cofinality', arXiv:2503.18898), Jakob solo ('Total Failure of Approachability...', arXiv:2508.02867), and Jakob–Poveda ('On Shelah's Approachability Ideal', arXiv:2508.04374) — solve long-standing Shelah/Foreman–Magidor/Mitchell questions by building GCH models where stationarily many points of cofinality μ (a regular cardinal *strictly below* λ, hence necessarily ≠ cf(λ) when λ has countable cofinality) are non-approachable. I confirmed via the abstracts that in every one of these papers the cofinality μ studied is a regular uncountable cardinal below the singular λ, distinct from cf(λ). Since Shelah's Theorem 1.8 already settles the CH_λ ⟺ ◇_S equivalence precisely on this different-cofinality regime, these 2025 results — however close in subject matter, and however much they resolve real open problems about approachability — are about a related-but-distinct question (approachability/goodness at cofinalities ≠ cf(λ)) and not a case of the stated problem (diamond at cofinality = cf(λ)). None of the papers I could access mention the diamond principle on E^{λ+}_{cf(λ)} specifically, and none claim to resolve or make partial progress on the exact same-cofinality entailment. I was unable to fully extract readable text from the PDF bodies of several papers (2508.04374, 2508.02867, and Zeman's 'Diamond, GCH and weak square') due to PDF compression issues with the fetch tool, relying instead on abstracts and secondary summarization of search results, which is a limitation on confidence. I did not find or open the frozen Wikipedia revision's own article text (no dedicated article exists for this specific bullet; it is one line among many in the 'List of unsolved problems in mathematics' Set theory section) nor the live article, since repeated WebFetch attempts on the full article were truncated before reaching the Set theory section. No AI system appears anywhere in any of these papers per the accessible content; there is no ai_role other than none.
competing_reading: One could argue the Jakob–Levine/Jakob/Jakob–Poveda approachability results are 'progress' in a loose sense, since approachability failure on a set is a necessary ingredient for diamond to fail there (non-membership in I[λ+] is required to even ask the diamond question meaningfully in some formulations), and these papers dramatically expand the known landscape of non-approachable configurations under GCH. If a future reader considers the family of these techniques (Namba-style forcing plus Levy collapse) as being 'the same neighborhood' as what would be needed to attack the cf(λ)=cf(λ) case, one might tag this as `progress`. I did not adopt this reading because none of the papers state, claim, or gesture at applicability to the exact same-cofinality set named in the bullet, and the scope rule (§3.1) requires the result to change what a careful person would write in this bullet's entry — it does not currently.
what_would_settle_it: A paper explicitly constructing a model (or proving in ZFC) that CH_λ holds for some singular λ while ◇ fails on some stationary S ⊆ E^{λ+}_{cf(λ)} (resolving it in the negative), or a ZFC proof that CH_λ always entails ◇ on this set (resolving it in the positive) — either dated after 26 January 2024 and either checked by an expert (for `resolved`) or merely posted (for `claimed`). Absent that, a partial result narrowing which λ or which sub-stationary-sets of E^{λ+}_{cf(λ)} the equivalence holds for (analogous to Zeman's weak-square-conditional result, but for a new class of λ) would count as `partial`.
